title: Add --env-path CLI flag (optional)
description:
## Background

Some users may want to customize the pool root without creating a config file. A CLI flag provides a simple override.

## Goal

Add `--env-path <DIR>` flag to treehouse CLI that sets the pool root directory.

## Scope

### CLI changes (main.rs)

Add flag to clap args:
```rust
/// Custom pool root directory (overrides treehouse.toml root and default ~/.treehouse)
#[arg(long = "env-path", value_name = "DIR")]
env_path: Option<PathBuf>,
```

### Core changes

When `--env-path` is provided:
1. Create a `CliEnv` that uses the specified directory as pool root
2. Pass it to `TreehouseCore::with_env()`
3. Skip config file loading (env path overrides config)

### Implementation

```rust
struct CliEnv {
    pool_root: PathBuf,
}

impl TreehouseEnv for CliEnv {
    fn pool_root(&self) -> Option<PathBuf> {
        Some(self.pool_root.clone())
    }
    // Delegate other methods to DefaultEnv
    fn read_file(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<String> { DefaultEnv.read_file(path) }
    fn write_file(&self, path: &Path, data: &[u8]) -> io::Result<()> { DefaultEnv.write_file(path, data) }
    // ... etc
}
```

## Considerations

- This is LOW PRIORITY — the trait API is the primary deliverable
- `--env-path` is a convenience for CLI users, not library consumers
- Should work with all subcommands (get, return, status, prune, destroy, gc)
- Does NOT override git operations — those still need a real repo
- Config file loading is skipped when `--env-path` is provided
- This bead depends on t52 (TreehouseCore wrapper)

## Tests

```rust
#[test]
fn cli_env_path_overrides_pool_root() {
    // Integration test: treehouse --env-path /tmp/pools status
}
```

## Validation

- `treehouse --env-path /tmp/pools status` works
- `treehouse --env-path /tmp/pools get` creates pool in custom location
- Existing CLI behavior unchanged when flag is absent
- `cargo clippy` clean
- `cargo test` passes

title: Wire TreehouseEnv into Pool struct
description:
## Background

The `Pool` struct is the primary entrypoint to treehouse-core. Current state:
- `pool.rs:92-98`: struct has `root`, `dir`, `git`, `process`, `config`, `lock_timeout`
- Constructor: `Pool::open(repo_root, remote_url, opts)`
- Internally calls: `State::read_state()`, `with_state_lock()`, `state_file::write_state()`
- All use hardcoded filesystem operations
- `gc.rs`, `prune.rs`, `destroy.rs` all create pools via `Pool::open()`
- `doctor.rs` reads state via `pool.pool_dir().join("treehouse-state.json")`

## Goal

Add an `env` field to `Pool` so all internal state operations go through the trait. Existing `Pool::open()` wraps `DefaultEnv`.

## Scope

### Pool struct changes

```rust
pub struct Pool {
    pub root: PathBuf,
    pub dir: PathBuf,
    pub(crate) git: Arc<dyn GitBackend>,
    pub(crate) process: Arc<ProcessTable>,
    pub(crate) config: TreehouseConfig,
    pub(crate) lock_timeout: std::time::Duration,
    pub(crate) env: Arc<dyn TreehouseEnv>,  // NEW
}
```

### New constructor

```rust
pub fn open_with_env(
    repo_root: &Path,
    remote_url: Option<&str>,
    opts: OpenOptions,
    env: Arc<dyn TreehouseEnv>,
) -> Result<Self, PoolError>
```

### Existing constructor (backward compatible)

```rust
pub fn open(repo_root, remote_url, opts) -> Result<Self, PoolError> {
    Self::open_with_env(repo_root, remote_url, opts, Arc::new(DefaultEnv))
}
```

### Internal wiring — all state operations go through env

Replace in Pool methods:
- `State::read_state(&self.dir)` → `State::read_state_with_env(&self.dir, &*self.env)`
- `with_state_lock(&self.dir, timeout, f)` → `with_state_lock_with_env(&self.dir, timeout, &*self.env, f)`
- `state_file::write_state(&self.dir, &state)` → `state_file::write_state_with_env(&self.dir, &state, &*self.env)`
- Process checks: `std::path::Path::new(&wt.path).exists()` → `self.env.path_exists(Path::new(&wt.path))`

### Accessor

```rust
pub fn env(&self) -> &dyn TreehouseEnv { &*self.env }
```

## Considerations

- `Arc<dyn TreehouseEnv>` for shared ownership across Pool methods
- Git operations (worktree add/remove/reset) still use filesystem directly — GitBackend trait handles that separately
- `doctor.rs` reads state file path via `pool.pool_dir().join("treehouse-state.json")` — this stays hardcoded (internal convention, not consumer-facing)
- `gc.rs`, `prune.rs`, `destroy.rs` call `Pool::open()` internally — they get DefaultEnv automatically, no changes needed
- Lock file is internal to pool_dir — consumer never interacts with it directly
- This bead depends on ALL Phase 1 beads (nq1, ckd, mhl, ivp)

## Tests

```rust
#[test]
fn pool_open_with_env_uses_injected_env() {
    let env = Arc::new(InMemoryEnv::new(PathBuf::from("/test/pools")));
    let pool_dir = PathBuf::from("/test/pools/myrepo-abc123");
    env.seed_file(&State::state_file_path(&pool_dir), b"{\"worktrees\":[]}");
    
    let config = TreehouseConfig::default_config();
    let pool = Pool::open_with_env(
        Path::new("/test/repo"),
        Some("https://github.com/x/y.git"),
        OpenOptions { config, lock_timeout: Duration::from_secs(5) },
        env.clone(),
    ).unwrap();
    
    assert_eq!(pool.env().pool_root(), Some(PathBuf::from("/test/pools")));
}

#[test]
fn pool_open_backward_compatible() {
    let dir = tempfile::tempdir().unwrap();
    let pool = Pool::open(dir.path(), None, OpenOptions::default()).unwrap();
    // pool.env() returns DefaultEnv
}
```

## Validation

- All existing Pool tests pass unchanged (DefaultEnv)
- New test: `Pool::open_with_env` with `InMemoryEnv`
- New test: `pool.env()` accessor returns correct env
- `cargo clippy` clean
- `cargo test` passes

title: Implement TreehouseEnv trait + DefaultEnv + InMemoryEnv
description:
## Background

treehouse-core currently hardcodes all filesystem paths and env var reads throughout the codebase. This prevents consumers from embedding treehouse as a library with custom storage (SQLite, S3, in-memory) and custom path resolution.

Key hardcoded locations (from grep analysis):
- `config.rs:164,176,178`: `home.join(".treehouse")`
- `config.rs:125`: `std::env::var_os("HOME")`
- `discovery.rs:39,59`: `h.join(".treehouse")`
- `updater.rs:88-92`: `std::env::var_os("HOME")` + ".treehouse/update-check.json"
- `state_file.rs`: all `std::fs::write` / `std::fs::read`
- `state.rs:141,146`: `pool_dir.join("treehouse-state.json")`
- `lock.rs`: `fd_lock` on lock file
- `git/shell.rs:117,143`: `std::env::var_os("GIT_BIN")`, `"PATH"`
- `hooks.rs:93`: `std::env::var("COMSPEC")`

## Goal

Create the foundational trait that abstracts ALL filesystem and environment side-effects, plus two implementations:
- `DefaultEnv`: identical to current behavior (real filesystem + env vars)
- `InMemoryEnv`: zero filesystem for tests

## Scope

### New file: `crates/treehouse-core/src/env.rs`

Define `TreehouseEnv` trait (must be `Send + Sync`) with these methods:

**Path resolution:**
- `pool_root(&self) -> Option<PathBuf>` — where pools live (default: `/Users/tranquangdang21/.treehouse`)
- `update_cache_path(&self) -> Option<PathBuf>` — update cache location (default: `~/.treehouse/update-check.json`)
- `user_config_path(&self) -> Option<PathBuf>` — user config file location (default: `~/.config/treehouse/config.toml`)

**Filesystem operations:**
- `read_file(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<String>`
- `read_bytes(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<Vec<u8>>`
- `write_file(&self, path: &Path, data: &[u8]) -> io::Result<()>` — atomic preferred
- `ensure_dir(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<()>`
- `path_exists(&self, path: &Path) -> bool`
- `list_dir(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<Vec<PathBuf>>`
- `file_meta(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<FileMeta>`

**Environment:**
- `env_var(&self, name: &str) -> Option<String>`
- `env_var_os(&self, name: &str) -> Option<PathBuf>`
- `cwd(&self) -> Option<PathBuf>`

Also define `FileMeta` struct (size: u64, modified: Option<SystemTime>).

### DefaultEnv

- Uses `std::fs::*` for all file operations
- Uses `std::env::var_os` for env vars
- `pool_root()`: `/Users/tranquangdang21/.treehouse` (existing behavior)
- `update_cache_path()`: `~/.treehouse/update-check.json`
- `user_config_path()`: `~/.config/treehouse/config.toml`
- `write_file()`: creates parent dirs automatically
- `list_dir()`: filters out errors, returns valid entries only

### InMemoryEnv

- `HashMap<PathBuf, Vec<u8>>` for files (behind `RwLock<>`)
- `HashMap<PathBuf, bool>` for dirs (behind `RwLock<>`)
- `HashMap<String, String>` for env vars (no lock needed — set at construction)
- Constructor: `InMemoryEnv::new(pool_root: PathBuf)`
- Builder: `.with_env(key, val)` for chaining
- `seed_file(path, content)` helper for test setup
- `list_dir()`: falls back to real `std::fs::read_dir` for simplicity

## Considerations

- Trait bound: `Send + Sync` (thread-safe across Pool methods)
- All methods take `&self` — interior mutability via RwLock for InMemoryEnv
- DefaultEnv::write_file creates parent dirs (matches existing behavior in state_file.rs)
- DefaultEnv::list_dir filters Err entries (matches existing behavior in discovery.rs)
- This is the FOUNDATION bead — all other beads depend on it
- Must be implemented first before any _with_env variants

## Tests

```rust
#[test]
fn in_memory_env_read_write_roundtrip() {
    let env = InMemoryEnv::new(PathBuf::from("/test"));
    env.seed_file(Path::new("/test/file.txt"), b"hello");
    assert_eq!(env.read_file(Path::new("/test/file.txt")).unwrap(), "hello");
    assert!(env.path_exists(Path::new("/test/file.txt")));
    assert!(!env.path_exists(Path::new("/test/missing.txt")));
}

#[test]
fn in_memory_env_list_dir() {
    let env = InMemoryEnv::new(PathBuf::from("/test"));
    env.seed_file(Path::new("/test/a.txt"), b"a");
    env.seed_file(Path::new("/test/b.txt"), b"b");
    let entries = env.list_dir(Path::new("/test")).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(entries.len(), 2);
}

#[test]
fn in_memory_env_env_var() {
    let env = InMemoryEnv::new(PathBuf::from("/test"))
        .with_env("HOME", "/fake/home");
    assert_eq!(env.env_var("HOME"), Some("/fake/home".to_string()));
    assert_eq!(env.env_var("MISSING"), None);
}

#[test]
fn default_env_pool_root_matches_current() {
    let env = DefaultEnv;
    let root = env.pool_root();
    assert!(root.unwrap().ends_with(".treehouse"));
}
```

## Validation

- Existing tests must pass unchanged (DefaultEnv is identical to current behavior)
- InMemoryEnv unit tests pass
- `cargo clippy` clean
- `cargo test` passes

description:
## Background

updater.rs handles self-update checks. Hardcoded locations:
- `cache_path()`: `home.join(".treehouse").join("update-check.json")` (line 92)
- `read_cache()`: `std::fs::read(&path)` (line 121)
- `write_cache()`: `std::fs::create_dir_all` + `std::fs::write` (line 151-153)
- Env var reads: `HOME` / `USERPROFILE` (line 88-89)

## Goal

Add `_with_env` variants that accept `&dyn TreehouseEnv`.

## Scope

### New functions

1. `cache_path_with_env(env: &dyn TreehouseEnv) -> Option<PathBuf>`
   - Returns `env.update_cache_path()`

2. `read_cache_with_env(env: &dyn TreehouseEnv) -> Option<UpdateCheckCache>`
   - Calls `cache_path_with_env(env)` then `env.read_bytes()`
   - Deserializes JSON

3. `write_cache_with_env(env: &dyn TreehouseEnv, latest: &str)`
   - Calls `cache_path_with_env(env)` then `env.ensure_dir()` + `env.write_file()`
   - Serializes to JSON

4. `is_cache_stale_with_env(current: &str, env: &dyn TreehouseEnv) -> bool`
   - Uses `read_cache_with_env`

5. `update_available_with_env(current: &str, env: &dyn TreehouseEnv) -> bool`
   - Uses `read_cache_with_env`

### Existing functions

Keep ALL existing functions unchanged.

## Considerations

- `check_latest()` uses `curl` subprocess — stays unchanged (network I/O, not filesystem)
- `CACHE_TTL` and `Version` are pure logic — no env dependency
- `InMemoryEnv` for update cache: write_file + read_bytes roundtrip

## Tests

```rust
#[test]
fn cache_path_with_env_returns_env_path() {

    assert_eq!(

    assert_eq!(cache.latest_version, "2.0.0");
}

fn read_cache_with_env_missing_returns_none() {
    let env = InMemoryEnv::new(PathBuf::from("/test"));
    assert!(read_cache_with_env(&env).is_none());
}
```

## Validation

- Unit test: `cache_path_with_env` returns `env.update_cache_path()`
- Unit test: write + read roundtrip with `InMemoryEnv`
- Unit test: missing cache returns None
- Existing tests unchanged
- `cargo clippy` clean

title: Implement atomic state file writer (state_file.rs)
description:
## Background
Go writes treehouse-state.json atomically (internal/pool/state.go atomicWriteFile): same-dir temp file (O_EXCL random suffix) -> fsync -> close -> platform commit (rename+dir-sync POSIX / ReplaceFileW or MoveFileEx MOVEFILE_WRITE_THROUGH Windows) -> preserve existing file mode. A crash mid-write must never leave a truncated/empty live file. The port MUST reproduce this.

## Technical Approach
- atomic_write_file(path, data, perm): use tempfile::NamedTempFile::new_in(same dir) -> write -> sync_all() (tempfile does NOT fsync on persist; must call explicitly) -> persist(target).
- tempfile::persist() = rename(2) on unix (atomic overwrite) and MoveFileExW + MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING on Windows (std::fs::rename FAILS on Windows when dest exists — this is why persist is used).
- Preserve existing target file mode: if target exists, match its mode before persist; new files use perm 0644.
- On Windows, tempfile persist lacks the parent-dir fsync (weaker durability than POSIX syncDirectory). Accept for P0 (parity); document. Do NOT reinvent ReplaceFileW unless a specific test demands it.
- write_state(pool_dir, state): json serialize (MarshalIndent-equivalent, 2-space) then atomic_write_file to <poolDir>/treehouse-state.json.
- Do NOT acquire the lock here — callers wrap read+mutate+write in one with_state_lock (see lock bead). State::save is never individually locked.

## Success Criteria
- No staging temp file remains after write
- Interrupted write (temp created, no rename) never touches live file
- Existing file mode preserved; new file respects perm
- Windows-safe overwrite semantics (persist, not std::fs::rename)

## Test Plan
- Unit: temp files cleaned up; mode preservation; write-after-corrupt-trigger doesn't lose data; concurrent writers serialize via lock (see lock bead tests)
- Port Go atomicWriteFile-related tests

## Considerations
- Never change an existing field's type/precision (schema drift, risk #8).
- A 0-byte live file is the classic crash artifact; reads treat it as corrupt (recovery bead), writes replace it atomically.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] No staging temp file remains after write
- [ ] Interrupted write (temp created, no rename) never touches live file
- [ ] Existing file mode preserved; new file respects perm
- [ ] Windows-safe overwrite semantics (persist, not std::fs::rename)

title: Add CI workflow (cargo fmt/clippy/test/build on Linux/macOS/Windows)
description:
## Background
The Go project runs CI on ubuntu/macos/windows (github/workflows/ci.yml): gofmt, go vet, tests, build. The Rust port must ship a CI workflow that runs cargo fmt/clippy/test/build on all three OSes so cross-platform correctness is verified (plan requires Linux/macOS/Windows support).

## Technical Approach
- .github/workflows/ci.yml (GitHub Actions):
  - jobs: format+lint on ubuntu: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -D warnings.
  - jobs: test+build on a matrix [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest, windows-latest]: actions/checkout@v4, dtolnay/rust-toolchain (or actions-rs) with the MSRV 1.88 stable toolchain, then cargo test --workspace and cargo build --workspace (release).
  - Use cargo cache (Swatinem/rust-cache) for speed.
  - Pin the toolchain to the workspace rust-version (1.88) so edition-2024 features are available.
  - Do NOT run clippy with --all-features if the toon git dep is not yet wired; scope it to default features until toon lands (or wire toon as a fixture in the CI by pinning the rev).
- Optionally a release workflow (release.yml) later: build release binaries per-OS + checksums.txt for the updater. P2 unless the updater bead needs it for e2e.
- Ensure the e2e suite (real git worktrees, process spawn) is in the test matrix and does not run tests in parallel where they are timing-sensitive.

## Success Criteria
- cargo fmt --check + cargo clippy -D warnings + cargo test + cargo build all pass on ubuntu/macos/windows in CI
- e2e tests run on all three OSes
- CI is fast (cargo cache)

## Test Plan
- The CI workflow IS the test infrastructure; validate by pushing and watching the matrix.

## Considerations
- Windows shell differences: use cross-platform actions steps, not bash-only.
- The e2e harness builds a helper binary; ensure the build step precedes the test step on all OSes.
- Keep clippy scope at default features until the toon dep is pinned (avoid a broken --all-features).
- Depends on the workspace scaffold.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] cargo fmt --check + cargo clippy -D warnings + cargo test + cargo build all pass on ubuntu/macos/windows in CI
- [ ] e2e tests run on all three OSes
- [ ] CI is fast (cargo cache)

title: Implement pure destroy/prune/gc classification (worktree.rs)
description:
## Background
The Go destroy/prune classification (internal/pool/destroy.go, prune.go) is the shared safety engine. A target can accumulate MULTIPLE classes (leased+dirty, etc.), each gated by its own --include-* flag. worktree.rs must be PURE classification — no disk, no git — so destroy, prune, and gc agree on 'disposable' by construction.

## Technical Approach
- struct WorktreeRef { name: String, path: String }
- enum DestroyClass { Disposable, Leased, InUse, Dirty, Unmerged, Unverified }
- struct ClassSet(u32 bitmask) with constants DISPOSABLE|LEASED|IN_USE|DIRTY|UNMERGED|UNVERIFIED; add()/contains()/has_unlanded().
- classify_for_destroy(entry, procs, checks) -> ClassSet following Go destroy.go:263-310 order:
  1. leased -> LEASED (detail 'held by <holder>' if set)
  2. in-use (owner_alive OR procs > 0) -> IN_USE; proc-scan error -> IN_USE with 'cannot check processes' (fail closed)
  3. backing repo missing -> UNVERIFIED, stop
  4. is_dirty error -> UNVERIFIED; dirty -> DIRTY
  5. default ref empty -> UNVERIFIED; is_head_merged_into_ref error -> UNVERIFIED; not merged -> UNMERGED
  6. else DISPOSABLE
- missing_flags(&ClassSet, opts) -> Vec<&'static str>: LEASED needs (allowLeased && opts.include_leased) else --include-leased; IN_USE needs --include-in-use; {DIRTY|UNMERGED|UNVERIFIED} needs --include-unlanded. Multiple classes -> every flag needed.
- analyze_idle_worktree(wt, options) -> (PruneWorktree, PruneSkipped, stale: bool, context): prune's per-candidate analysis (orphan, dirty, merged, size).
- helper predicates: backing_repository_missing(wt) -> (bool, detail) via the linked-worktree .git file's gitdir pointer; linked_worktree_git_dir(wt); removable_worktree_container(path) — refuses unsafe roots.

## Success Criteria
- destroy/prune/gc all use this one classifier (same inputs -> same 'disposable')
- Multi-class targets require ALL corresponding flags
- Proc-scan failure and unresolvable default ref both classify UNVERIFIED (fail closed), never disposable
- A live surviving process is never classified disposable even with --include-in-use (process must actually terminate)

## Test Plan
- Unit: exhaustive ClassSet gating matrix (each class, combined classes, allowLeased true/false)
- Port Go internal/pool tests covering destroy classification gates (leased+dirty needs both flags; proc-scan-fail -> in-use/detail; surviving process never destroyed)
- e2e agreement: destroy and prune classify the same fixture identically

## Considerations
- This is the 'destroy and prune agree' invariant — the same-verbs-same-primitives rule from the audit.
- Never do I/O here; inputs are passed in so the layer stays pure and unit-testable.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] destroy/prune/gc all use this one classifier (same inputs -> same 'disposable')
- [ ] Multi-class targets require ALL corresponding flags
- [ ] Proc-scan failure and unresolvable default ref both classify UNVERIFIED (fail closed), never disposable
- [ ] A live surviving process is never classified disposable even with --include-in-use (process must actually terminate)

title: Implement CLI commands (clap): get/enter/return/status/prune/destroy/init/update/version
description:
## Background
crates/treehouse is the CLI binary crate (clap derive). It calls treehouse-core and renders results via the Formatter. The Go CLI contract (plan Appendix B) must be reproduced: exit codes, stdout/stderr routing, human message strings (byte-exact where Go-tested). main.rs is the error boundary: fn main -> anyhow::Result<()>; the error is printed ONCE to stderr, exit 1. NOTE: the self-update machinery (treehouse update + hidden --update-check background check) is a separate subsystem covered by the updater bead; this bead wires the CLI wiring only (flag + dispatch + banner + cache read), not the download/verify/atomic-replace internals.

## Technical Approach
- clap derive structs for each subcommand; --format human|json|toon is a GLOBAL arg (global=true, default human) accepted by get/return/status/prune/destroy/gc/doctor/run; REJECTED by init/update/enter/--version. --json stays a per-command bool alias exactly where Go has it (get, status).
- Resolution: --json -> Json; else --format value; else Human. Conflict (--json + --format != json) -> error 'conflicting output formats: --json and --format <v>' exit 1. get --json without --lease -> '--json requires --lease' byte-exact; get --format json/toon without --lease -> '--format json/toon requires --lease' (distinct).
- Commands (each calls core + Formatter):
  - get (also bare `treehouse`): interactive -> subshell (stdout EMPTY; spawn $SHELL else /bin/sh, win %COMSPEC% else cmd.exe; set TREEHOUSE_DIR=<abs wt>; on exit detach HEAD; dirty -> prompt 'Clean worktree and return to pool? [Y/n]'; declined -> 'Worktree left dirty. Use '\''treehouse return --force'\'' to clean it later.' exit 0); --lease -> stdout bare path (one line) or --json/--format object; banners to stderr.
  - enter <name>: --print-path -> stdout bare path only; else subshell, pool state untouched, 'Pool state unchanged.'
  - return [path]: --force, --if-lease-id, --if-lease-id empty -> error; dirty prompt unless --force; declined -> 'Aborted.' exit 0; conditional -> release_conditional.
  - status: human table -> stdout; --json array -> stdout; empty pool -> 'No worktrees in pool.' stderr exit 0; --format toon.

title: Implement config.rs (repo+user treehouse.toml merging + pool dir resolution)
description:
## Background
Go internal/config/config.go loads repo treehouse.toml and user ~/.config/treehouse/config.toml (on Windows %USERPROFILE%). Repo config takes precedence for repo-safe settings; Hooks are loaded ONLY from user config (repo hooks are ignored for safety). LoadGlobal ignores repo config because it may run without a repo.

## Technical Approach
- struct TreehouseConfig { max_trees: u32 (default 16), root: Option<String>, hooks: Hooks }
- struct Hooks { post_create: Vec<String>, pre_destroy: Vec<String> } (serde, omitempty)
- struct UserConfig { max_trees, root, hooks }
- load(repo_root) -> Config:
  - start from DefaultConfig (max_trees 16)
  - if <repo_root>/treehouse.toml exists: decode it (error on parse failure), then CLEAR hooks (cfg.Hooks = empty) — repo hooks are ignored for safety
  - load user config (~/.config/treehouse/config.toml via dirs or $HOME/.config/treehouse/config.toml); if repo config present, merge only hooks from user config; else user config is authoritative
- load_global() -> Config: DefaultConfig merged with user config ONLY (no repo config).
- ResolvePoolDir(repo_root, root) -> poolDir: hashInput = git remote URL (origin) if available else abs repo path; short_hash = first 6 hex of sha256(hashInput); poolName = repoName + "-" + short_hash; poolDir = ResolvePoolRoot(repo_root, root) + "/" + poolName.
- ResolvePoolRoot(repo_root, root): root=="" -> $HOME/.treehouse; expand env vars (os.ExpandEnv); relative root requires repo (else error); absolute or expanded nests under given root + "/.treehouse".
- ConfigError enum: Invalid(path, msg), Io, Toml.

## Success Criteria
- Repo + user config merge matches Go precedence (repo wins repo-safe settings; hooks only from user)
- Repo hooks are never executed (ignored)
- Pool dir resolution: empty root -> $HOME/.treehouse/{repo}-{hash}; relative/./ roots nest under repo; absolute + $VAR-expanded nest under given root; relative root without repo fails
- load_global ignores repo config
- P1: config gains lease_ttl: Option<Duration> (run's default TTL)

## Test Plan

title: Implement corrupt-state recovery (recovery.rs)
description:
## Background
Go recoverCorruptState (internal/pool/state.go) runs when treehouse-state.json exists but fails to parse. It must NOT brick the pool: it scans on-disk worktrees and marks every recovered entry as leased (conservative), fails closed if the scan cannot complete. The port MUST mirror this exactly — a 0-byte file is corrupt, only a missing file is fresh.

## Technical Approach
- recover_corrupt_state(pool_dir, parse_err) -> Result<State, StateError>:
  - FAIL CLOSED: if os::ReadDir of the pool or any slot fails, return error (never an incomplete state).
  - Scan: every dir under pool_dir is a slot; every dir under a slot is a candidate worktree; candidate included only if <path>/.git exists.
  - Recovered entry: Name=slot, Path=slot/worktree, CreatedAt=now, Leased=true, LeaseHolder=const RECOVERED_LEASE_HOLDER = "recovered: state file was corrupt or truncated; verify before reuse", LeasedAt=now, NO owner, NO lease_id, NO expires_at (permanent lease so gc can never auto-reclaim — deliberate conservative mirror).
- Print a LOUD warning to stderr containing "corrupt or truncated", telling the user to run treehouse status then treehouse return or treehouse destroy --include-leased.
- Acquire and prune skip recovered (leased) entries; destroy only removes via a single named --include-leased target.
- Missing state file = State{worktrees:[]} (fresh), not an error, NOT recovery.

## Success Criteria
- Corrupt/truncated/empty-but-present file recovers conservatively, never hands out a worktree
- Unreadable slot -> hard error (fail closed), state NOT rewritten
- Missing file -> fresh empty pool
- stderr warning contains 'corrupt or truncated'
- Recovered entries are leased with the exact placeholder holder and no expires_at

## Test Plan
- Port Go TestPruneAllYesRecoversCorruptPoolWithoutDeletingItsWorktree + internal/pool/state_test.go recovery cases
- Unit: unreadable slot (chmod 0 on unix, non-root) fails closed; 0-byte file => recovery
- e2e: corrupt one pool's state among several => prune --all still works, other pools unaffected

## Considerations
- On Windows the slot-scan has no direct test coverage in Go; add Rust coverage.
- Recovery only fires for an existing-but-unparsable file.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Corrupt/truncated/empty-but-present file recovers conservatively, never hands out a worktree
- [ ] Unreadable slot -> hard error (fail closed), state NOT rewritten
- [ ] Missing file -> fresh empty pool
- [ ] stderr warning contains 'corrupt or truncated'
- [ ] Recovered entries are leased with the exact placeholder holder and no expires_at

title: P1-C: treehouse doctor (read-only health report, 12 checks, --format + --strict)
description:
## Background
treehouse doctor is a READ-ONLY health report (never mutates state; never heals, never writes). It answers: why is this worktree still here? why can't treehouse reclaim it? is an agent still using it? is state broken? Flags: --format human|json|toon, --strict (any warn also fails). Exit 0 when no error-severity check; 1 when any error; --strict promotes warns to failing.

## Technical Approach
- enum Severity { Ok, Warn, Error }
- struct DoctorCheck { name: &'static str, status: Severity, detail: String, count: u64, bytes: Option<u64>, affected: Vec<PathBuf> }
- struct DoctorReport { checks: Vec<DoctorCheck>, healthy: bool, strict_healthy: bool } (healthy = no Error; strict_healthy = no Warn|Error)
- enum Format { Human, Json, Toon }; struct DoctorOptions { format, strict }
- run_doctor(env, opts) -> Result<DoctorReport> — READ-ONLY; probes only; a single short exclusive state lock only for state health.
- 12 CHECKS:
  1. git_binary — Error if `git --version` fails
  2. config — Error if repo/user config fails to parse; Error if pool-dir resolution fails; Warn if no config
  3. state — Error if treehouse-state.json exists but unparsable (recovery would apply; detail 'corrupt or truncated' + would-recover count); Ok if missing or parses
  4. state_writable — Error if a probe temp file can't be created+written+removed in pool dir
  5. lock — Error if treehouse-state.lock can't be opened/locked (probe acquire+release; advisory locks auto-release on death, so no stale locks); Warn if anomalously large
  6. dead_owners — Warn (count + paths) where owner reservation no longer matches a live process; detail: heal would clear on next status/gc/run
  7. stale_leases — Warn (count + bytes) for leased && expired, plus a separate reclaimable count (those that also pass the disposable bar -> safe gc --yes candidates)
  8. active_leases — informational Ok count of valid leases
  9. orphans — Warn for backing-repository-missing linked worktrees
  10. dirty — Warn per worktree with uncommitted tracked/untracked changes (--untracked-files=all)
  11. in_use — Warn per worktree with a live process inside or a live owner reservation
  12. disk — Ok with used/bytes; Warn when free disk < 10% of total on the pool volume
- OUTPUT MODEL (json, one compact object + newline on stdout): {"healthy":true,"strict_healthy":false,"checks":[...]} — all findings to stdout; only doctor-fails-to-run errors (not in repo, cannot resolve pool root, cannot load config) -> stderr + exit 1.
- HUMAN: 'treehouse doctor' header then one line per check using check markers: '  ✓ git binary: git 2.47.0' / '  ⚠ stale leases: 2 (1 reclaimable, 12.5 MiB)' / '  ✗ state: corrupt or truncated ...'; then summary 'Doctor: <e> error(s), <w> warning(s)'. toon renders the same compactly.

## Success Criteria
- doctor is read-only (never writes state, never heals)
- 12 exact checks with correct severity; exit 0/1 only; --strict promotes warns
- JSON/TOON output on stdout; all findings included; actionable detail suggests remedies
- A dirty worktree left by an agent does NOT fail the default run (warn only)

## Test Plan
- Unit: severity logic; exit-code mapping; --strict promotion
- e2e: doctor against healthy pool (exit 0), corrupt state (exit 1 + 'corrupt or truncated'), missing git (exit 1), stale lease (exit 0 default, exit 1 --strict), disk-low warn
- Golden: doctor --json / --format toon fixtures

## Considerations
- The in-use process scan is the most expensive check; on large systems gc --all over many pools may take seconds (optional --verbose diagnostics exist).
- doctor reports what heal WOULD clear and never writes — matches the conservative-action principle.
- Markers: use '  ✓' / '  ⚠' / '  ✗' (two-space indent + glyph) in human output; these are cosmetic, not contract — do not assert them byte-exact in scripts.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] doctor is read-only (never writes state, never heals)
- [ ] 12 exact checks with correct severity; exit 0/1 only; --strict promotes warns
- [ ] JSON/TOON output on stdout; all findings included; actionable detail suggests remedies
- [ ] A dirty worktree left by an agent does NOT fail the default run (warn only)

title: Implement GitBackend trait + ShellGitBackend (git/mod.rs, git/shell.rs)
description:
## Background
Go shells out to the git binary (internal/git/git.go) — go-git has incomplete worktree support, so the Rust port must also shell out. Define an object-safe Send+Sync trait so a native gix backend can be swapped in later (NOT P0). ShellGitBackend spawns git.exe DIRECTLY (no shell, no quoting — MSVC CRT rules handle spaces).

## Technical Approach
- trait GitBackend: Send + Sync, methods mirroring Go git.go (each with the exact git invocation):
  - repo_root(start) -> PathBuf (rev-parse --show-toplevel; FindMainRepoRootFrom resolves the main repo root for linked worktrees)
  - default_branch(repo) -> String (origin/HEAD symbolic-ref -> local symbolic-ref HEAD -> init.defaultBranch -> error)
  - fetch(repo) -> () no-op without origin; must fail with kind OriginUnreachable so prune can emit a category-tagged skip (NOT a deletion)
  - worktree_add(repo, path, base) / worktree_remove(repo, path, force) (force for destroy, plain for prune-clean)
  - is_dirty(wt) -> bool: `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` — ANY output == dirty; the --untracked-files=all flag is load-bearing (forces untracked inclusion past status.showUntrackedFiles)
  - reset_worktree(wt, reference): `git checkout --detach --force <ref>` then `git reset --hard <ref>` then `git clean -fd` — must remain a single semantic unit (port of ResetWorktree)
  - is_head_merged_into_ref(wt, reference): `git merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD <ref>`; exit 0 merged, exit 1 NOT merged (NOT an error), other exits -> kind StatusFailed so destroy marks Unverified
  - default_branch_merge_ref(repo, origin): origin repos `git ls-remote --symref origin HEAD`, then require refs/remotes/origin/<branch> exists AND SHA == remote HEAD SHA, else fail closed (stale); local-only repos use refs/heads/<default>, fail closed if unresolvable
  - branch_ref(wt): branchRef — strictly-ahead ref wins, origin on divergence, whichever exists otherwise
- struct GitRepo { common_dir: PathBuf, worktree: Option<PathBuf> }
- ShellGitBackend { git_bin: PathBuf, env: Vec<(OsString,OsString)> }:
  - discover(): GIT_BIN env -> PATH -> Windows Program Files\Git\bin\git.exe
  - run(args, cwd) -> Output; run_checked(args,cwd,kind) -> exit-code check + stderr capture into GitError::Exit{code,stderr,kind}; run_stdout(args,cwd) -> trimmed UTF-8-lossy stdout
- GitError enum (thiserror) with GitErrorKind category tags: NotFound, DefaultBranchUnresolvable, OriginUnreachable, MergeRefUnresolvable, StatusFailed, Other.

## Success Criteria
- All git invocations produce Go-identical behavior (same commands, same exit-code interpretation)
- is_dirty forces --untracked-files=all
- is_head_merged_into_ref treats exit 1 as NOT merged, not error
- ShellGitBackend spawns git directly (never a shell); works on Windows with spaces in paths
- fetch failure categorizes as OriginUnreachable

## Test Plan
- Unit (mock-free, real git): each method against a temp repo + bare remote
- Port Go internal/git/git_test.go cases (default branch resolution, merge ref staleness, detached linked worktree, RemoveCleanWorktree rejects dirty, IsDirty with status.showUntrackedFiles=no)

## Considerations
- Windows: pass each arg as its own OsString; never shell-quote. Use Path throughout for separators.
- reset_worktree force-deletes untracked files — the TOCTOU window is addressed at the pool layer (reservation), not here.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] All git invocations produce Go-identical behavior (same commands, same exit-code interpretation)
- [ ] is_dirty forces --untracked-files=all
- [ ] is_head_merged_into_ref treats exit 1 as NOT merged, not error
- [ ] ShellGitBackend spawns git directly (never a shell); works on Windows with spaces in paths
- [ ] fetch failure categorizes as OriginUnreachable

title: Implement hooks runner (hooks.rs)
description:
## Background
Go internal/hooks/hooks.go runs user-configured shell commands at lifecycle points. Commands run sequentially in the worktree dir via the OS shell (/bin/sh -c on unix, %COMSPEC% /d /s /c on windows). A failing hook is logged but does not stop later hooks or fail the caller. post_create runs AFTER the state lock is released (must not deadlock). pre_destroy runs OUTSIDE all locks.

## Technical Approach
- struct HooksRunner { shell: Shell } where Shell resolves per-platform.
- run(commands, work_dir, stdout, stderr): for each command, run_one sequentially.
- run_one(command, work_dir, stdout, stderr): build shell command; on failure log to stderr: tree emoji hook command failed: "<cmd>" (exit N): <err> — never fail the caller.
- Shell resolution: unix /bin/sh -c <cmd>; windows %COMSPEC% /d /s /c <cmd> (COMSPEC fallback cmd.exe). Use the exact windowsShellCommandLine double-quote wrapping the Go test pins (a single exact-string test).
- IMPORTANT: hooks run with cwd set to the target worktree dir; they must run OUTSIDE the state lock (a probe acquiring WithStateLock from inside the hook must succeed within 500ms — port the Go test).
- post_create hook stdout: interactive get lets it go to stdout; LEASE mode routes it to STDERR so machine output stays clean.
- pre_destroy hooks run before delete; re-run of classification after hooks is the destroy/prune/gc layer's job.

## Success Criteria
- Hooks run in order; a failing hook logs and continues; empty list is a no-op
- Hooks run with cwd = worktree dir
- post_create does NOT hold the state lock (no deadlock probe)
- Lease mode routes hook stdout to stderr

## Test Plan
- Port Go internal/hooks/hooks_test.go: order, failure-continue, empty list, cwd, and the post_create-does-not-hold-lock probe (re-exec test binary with TREEHOUSE_HOLD_CWD_PROBE)
- Windows: the exact cmd.exe /d /s /c double-quote wrapping string test
- e2e: get --lease with a post_create hook writing to stdout stays clean on stdout

## Considerations
- Windows quoting beyond the one pinned case is untested in Go; keep the exact string.
- Hooks are user-level only (config bead enforces).
- Do NOT run git or hooks under the state lock (short-lock protocol).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Hooks run in order; a failing hook logs and continues; empty list is a no-op
- [ ] Hooks run with cwd = worktree dir
- [ ] post_create does NOT hold the state lock (no deadlock probe)
- [ ] Lease mode routes hook stdout to stderr

title: Implement Lease (lease.rs): durable process-independent reservation
description:
## Background
Go durable leases (internal/pool/state.go, pool.go) are a process-independent reservation: leased=true + lease_id + lease_holder + leased_at, with NO owner reservation. A lease survives zero processes, is NEVER cleared by heal_state, is skipped by Acquire and prune, and is cleared only by Release. Lease_id is a fresh 128-bit hex per acquisition. Conditional release is ABA-safe under one lock.

## Technical Approach
- struct Lease { id: String, holder: String, acquired_at: DateTime<Utc>, expires_at: Option<DateTime<Utc>> } — expires_at is P1 (None = permanent lease, matches Go's zero = permanent).
- impl Lease:
  - write_to(&self, e: &mut WorktreeEntry): stamp the flattened Go fields (Leased=true, LeaseID=id, LeaseHolder=holder, LeasedAt=acquired_at, OwnerPID=0, OwnerStartedAt=0, expires_at if set) — this is what markAcquired does in Go.
  - from_entry(e, ttl): reconstitute from a state entry; expires_at re-derived only from an in-memory map (never read from file in P0 — Go files have no TTL).
- mark_acquired(wt, lease): when lease mode, generate new_lease_id() (16 rand bytes -> 32 lowercase hex), set Leased=true + fields, zero the owner pair; otherwise reserve_owner.
- clear_lease(wt): Leased=false, id/holder="", leased_at=zero, expires_at=zero.
- LeaseError enum: PreconditionFailed{expected,exp_holder,actual,act_holder} (Go ErrLeasePreconditionFailed), NotFound(String), Expired(String, DateTime), Rng(String).

## Success Criteria
- A lease is recorded with no owner reservation (owner_pid/owner_started_at zero)
- Lease survives with zero processes (never cleared by heal)
- lease_id is fresh per acquisition even for same path/holder
- Lease fields serialize with omitempty/omitzero (leased_at omitted when zero)
- clear_lease returns the entry to a fully-unleased state

## Test Plan
- Unit: mark_acquired lease vs owner; write_to round-trip; clear_lease; new_lease_id format (32 hex)
- Port Go lease-related state tests + e2e TestGetLeaseAndStatusJSONContracts (lease_id 128-bit hex, leased_at populated)
- ABA conditional-release behavior is covered by the pool acquire/release bead.

## Considerations
- P1 adds expires_at and --ttl; keep the field additive (zero = permanent) so pre-P1 state files load identically.
- A lease id is immutable per acquisition; never reuse.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A lease is recorded with no owner reservation (owner_pid/owner_started_at zero)
- [ ] Lease survives with zero processes (never cleared by heal)
- [ ] lease_id is fresh per acquisition even for same path/holder
- [ ] Lease fields serialize with omitempty/omitzero (leased_at omitted when zero)
- [ ] clear_lease returns the entry to a fully-unleased state

title: Implement output layer: CommandResult + Formatter (human/json/toon)
description:
## Background
The output layer turns a single structured CommandResult per command into human/json/toon. Plan principle: core produces one CommandResult and serializes it to serde_json::Value; the CLI turns that Value into JSON or TOON. Core never knows what TOON is — the abstraction boundary is CommandResult -> serde_json::Value -> { JSON, TOON }.

## Technical Approach
- treehouse-core/src/result.rs: enum CommandResult { Get(GetResult), Enter(EnterResult), Return(ReturnResult), Status(Vec<WorktreeStatus>), Prune(PruneResult), Destroy(DestroyResult), Gc(GcResult), Doctor(DoctorResult), Run(RunResult) } with payload() -> Option<serde_json::Value> (None for interactive get/enter so stdout stays empty).
- Serde structs with snake_case, Go wire names:
  - LeaseInfo { path, lease_id, lease_holder, leased_at } (4 keys always present, leased_at non-null; P1 adds expires_at)
  - WorktreeStatus { name, path, status, lease_id, lease_holder, leased_at: Option<String>, processes: Vec<Process> } — ALL keys always present; lease_id/lease_holder "" when not leased; leased_at null when not leased; processes [] when none. P1 adds expires_at + stale.
  - ReturnResult { path, returned, aborted, terminated: Vec<Process>, warnings: Vec<String> } (NEW schema)
  - PruneResult { dry_run, orphans_included, global, pool_count, candidates, pruned, skipped, reclaimable_bytes, freed_bytes, pool_root? , pools? } (NEW)
  - DestroyResult { dry_run, all, scope, planned, destroyed, skipped, planned_bytes, freed_bytes } (NEW)
  - GcResult / DoctorResult { healthy, strict_healthy, checks } (NEW)
  - CommandError::SingleDestroySkipped { name, class, flags, detail } whose Display = 'did not destroy <name> (<class>); re-run with <flags>'.
- treehouse-cli/src/format.rs: trait Formatter { fn render(&self, result, out: &mut dyn Write, err: &mut dyn Write) }; impl HumanFormatter, JsonFormatter, ToonFormatter. formatter(OutputFormat) -> Box<dyn Formatter>.
- stdout/stderr discipline: machine data (bare path/JSON/TOON) -> out ONLY; tree emoji banners/warnings/prompts -> err in EVERY format. Errors -> stderr once, exit 1.
- ToonFormatter: payload -> serde_json::to_value -> toon::encode(v, None) -> writeln (encode emits NO trailing newline).
- Banner rules (emit_banners) per format: Get(Lease) banner in every format; Status empty -> human ONLY 'No worktrees in pool.' (json/toon print none); Return banners; Prune/Destroy summaries are the human payload (stdout in human, structured otherwise); warnings to stderr always.
- Colors (status green/red/yellow/magenta/cyan+bold; updated green) via owo-colors, auto-disabled off-TTY.

## Success Criteria
- JSON byte-stable: status empty exactly '[]\n'; lease_id/lease_holder always present; leased_at null when not leased; processes always present
- get --lease --json 4 keys always present, leased_at non-null
- TOON round-trips to the same data as JSON (toon::try_decode in tests)

title: P1-A: Short-lock protocol + reservation revalidation + lock timeout + Windows termination design
description:
## Background
The Go audit found: (1) long lock holds — git reset, process termination, and deletion run UNDER the lock, so a hung git/hook stalls every other pool command; (2) a TOCTOU where reset+clean -fd races a newly-entering process; (3) abrupt Windows termination; (4) no lock timeout (Go blocks forever on flock). P1-A formalizes the short-lock protocol the P0 pool already structures.

## Technical Approach
- SHORT-LOCK PROTOCOL: move git reset/clean, git worktree add/remove, IsDirty/merged checks, hooks, and process cwd-scan+kill OUTSIDE the state lock in acquire/release/destroy/prune/gc. Reservation tokens are PERSISTED (owner pair / Destroying+owner / lease_id), so they survive lock releases and are re-validated under a re-acquired lock via Reservation::matches().
- ACQUIRE becomes: [L] reserve (ms) -> reset OUTSIDE -> [L] commit (re-read + validate token intact). RELEASE: [L] precond+callback -> reset OUTSIDE -> [L] clear. RELEASE_CONDITIONAL stays ONE lock (ABA-safe). DESTROY/PRUNE/GC: [L] reserve -> hooks OUTSIDE -> [L] verify+delete. STATUS: ONE exclusive lock (heals+scans+writes). DOCTOR: no lock (probes) or a single short exclusive lock.
- TOCTOU closure: stamp the reservation BEFORE the external reset so any treehouse consumer entering mid-reset sees owner_alive and skips; keep the reservation across return so destroy can't delete a mid-reset worktree; re-validate the persisted token at commit. Residual (documented): a bare non-treehouse process cd'ing in during reset is unprotected (only cooperative consumers coordinated).
- LOCK TIMEOUT: try_lock + retry/backoff up to lock_timeout -> StateError::LockTimeout (Go blocks forever; this is a deliberate deviation, documented, default a few seconds).
- WINDOWS TERMINATION: document/design — abrupt TerminateProcess is the only cross-platform kill; prefer graceful/git-level shutdown before TerminateProcess where possible; survivors under --include-in-use must restore + skip, never delete.
- GO-RUST MIXED-POOL OWNER-LIVENESS: Go stores CreateTime millis; sysinfo returns seconds; store millis (accept truncation) and document that mixed Go+Rust concurrency on one pool is unsupported.
- RECOVERY + CONCURRENCY TESTS: race tests (6-way double-lease, exactly-once conditional release, concurrent destroy+acquire, acquire during destroy hook), corrupt-state recovery tests, crash-between-D1-and-D2 (Destroying + dead owner) self-heal.

## Success Criteria
- No git/hooks/process operation runs under the state lock
- Persisted reservation revalidation closes the TOCTOU for cooperative consumers
- Lock timeout turns a wedged holder into LockTimeout (not infinite block)
- Windows termination design documented + survivors never deleted
- Race tests pass; corrupt-state + crash-mid-destroy recovery verified

## Test Plan
- Race tests: two acquire never double-issue; two ReleaseConditional exactly-once; destroy vs re-acquire during hook
- Recovery: corrupt state among pools; crash between destroy phase 1 and 2 self-heals (Destroying cleared when owner dead)
- Lock: wedged holder times out; lock released after panic/error
- Port Go concurrency probes (re-exec test binary with TREEHOUSE_HOLD_CWD_PROBE)

## Considerations
- This is the deliberate fix for the audit's 'long lock holds' risk; the extra re-acquire per operation is the accepted cost.
- Do not regress the ABA-safety of release_conditional — it stays one lock.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] No git/hooks/process operation runs under the state lock
- [ ] Persisted reservation revalidation closes the TOCTOU for cooperative consumers
- [ ] Lock timeout turns a wedged holder into LockTimeout (not infinite block)
- [ ] Windows termination design documented + survivors never deleted
- [ ] Race tests pass; corrupt-state + crash-mid-destroy recovery verified

title: Implement pool acquire/release/status (pool.rs)
description:
## Background
pool.rs is the orchestrator and the only public entrypoint to treehouse-core. It implements acquire (get), release (return), release_conditional, status (list). The SHORT-LOCK PROTOCOL is the target: git/hooks/process work runs OUTSIDE the lock; the reservation is stamped BEFORE the external reset and re-validated after (persisted reservation token). This closes the audit's 'long lock holds' risk. Go held the lock during git reset (correct but stalls every other command); the Rust port deliberately does not.

## Technical Approach
- struct Pool { root, dir, state_path, lock_path, git: Arc<dyn GitBackend>, process: Arc<ProcessTable>, config, lock_timeout }
- struct Acquired { name, path: PathBuf, branch, lease: Option<Lease> }
- pub fn open(repo_root, opts) -> Result<Self>: resolve poolDir = config::resolve_pool_dir(repo_root, cfg.root) -> <root>/.treehouse/<repoName>-<6hexsha256(url-or-path)>; MkdirAll 0755.
- get(&self, opts: AcquireOptions) -> Result<Acquired> (ACQUIRE):
  1. OUTSIDE lock: default_branch (git); if HasRemote origin, fetch.
  2. SHORT LOCK #1 (reserve): read_state + heal_state; scan entries skipping Destroying/Leased/owner_alive; skip if process in use (find_in_worktree) or IsDirty; pick candidate; mark_acquired (reserve_owner OR lease.write_to) + WriteState. The reservation is now PERSISTED (owner pair / lease fields) — any concurrent treehouse consumer sees owner_alive==true and skips. If no available worktree and pool < max_trees: create new (MkdirAll + git worktree add --detach <path> <branchRef>) + mark_acquired + append + WriteState.
  3. OUTSIDE lock: git reset_worktree (checkout --detach --force -> reset --hard -> clean -fd) — the reservation held since step 2 is the anti-TOCTOU wall.
  4. SHORT LOCK #2 (commit): re-read; validate the reservation token still intact (owner/lease fields unchanged); WriteState only if heal changed something.
  5. OUTSIDE lock: run post_create hooks (lease mode routes stdout to stderr).
  - P0 STOPGAP: if the two-lock acquire proves too complex to land correct in P0, reset MAY run inside lock #2 for Go-parity (simplest correct). If so, flag it explicitly and P1-A migrates it out — the final state MUST be short-lock. Do NOT ship both.
- AcquireOptions { branch: Option<String>, create: bool, lease: Option<LeaseAcquireOptions>, before_reset: Option<Box<dyn FnMut(&WorktreeEntry) + Send>> }.
- AcquireLease / AcquireLeaseInfo: non-interactive; leases; returns LeaseInfo { path, lease_id, lease_holder, leased_at } (+ P1 expires_at).
- release(&self, target, opts) (RELEASE): repo/branch resolution OUTSIDE; INSIDE one lock: releasable_worktree (must be managed, not Destroying) -> run before_reset callback (UNDER the lock, per Go doc — caller's termination/detachment cannot race a later acquisition) -> clear owner + clear_lease -> WriteState. git reset_worktree runs OUTSIDE (before or after the lock; the reservation held across it).
- release_conditional(&self, target, expected) -> ONE lock: validate preconditions (LeaseError::PreconditionFailed on mismatch, no mutation) -> before_reset -> reset -> clear -> WriteState (ABA-safe, exactly-once under concurrency). Do NOT split this — ABA-safety requires the whole check+clear in one lock.
- ValidateReleasePreconditions: read-only check under lock.
- status(&self) -> Vec<WorktreeStatus>: ONE exclusive lock: read+heal+WriteState; for each entry compute status: leased -> 'leased' (with id/holder/leased_at); owner_alive -> 'in-use'; processes>0 -> 'in-use' (and 'you're here' if cwd inside); dirty -> 'dirty'; else 'available'. Skip Destroying entries. Status values exactly: available|in-use|dirty|leased|you're here.
- next_name(state): max numeric name + 1.
- PoolError enum: LeasedBulk{name}, InUse{name}, Unlanded{name}, ReAcquiredDuringHook{name}, BeingDestroyed{name}, NotFound(name), Leased(name).

## Success Criteria
- get never hands out a leased, dirty, in-use, or Destroying worktree
- A reused worktree is reset to the latest default branch (branchRef: prefer-ahead/local, origin on divergence)
- release clears owner + lease and returns the worktree to available; conditional release is ABA-safe exactly-once
- status heals + writes state under the lock, and classifies into exactly the 5 Go statuses
- A dirty-prompt decline path exists at the CLI layer (not core)
- The 'you're here' status only when cwd is inside the worktree
- NO git/hooks/process work runs under the state lock (short-lock target)

## Test Plan
- Port Go internal/pool/pool_test.go: acquire reuse, leased skip, dirty skip, owner heal, nextName
- e2e (cmd/e2e_test.go): TestGetAndStatus, TestGetReusesWorktree, TestGetLeasePrintsOnlyPathToStdout, TestGetLeaseRecordsHolder, TestReturnLegacyPathOnly, TestReturnConditionalLeaseIdentityLifecycle (ABA), TestReturnConditionalDirtyPromptDoesNotHoldPoolLock
- Concurrency: two concurrent acquire never hand out the same worktree (6-way double-lease test)

## Considerations
- The reservation IS the anti-TOCTOU wall: stamp it before the external reset, keep it across return, re-validate at commit. A bare non-treehouse process cd'ing in during reset is unprotected (only cooperative consumers coordinated) — residual, documented, same as Go.
- Do NOT hold the lock during post_create hooks or process termination.
- Releasing holds one lock for precondition+reset+clear — required for ABA-safety; do not split it.
- P1-A formalizes the short-lock protocol + lock timeout; P0 must already structure acquire/release this way (no reset under lock) to avoid a P1-A rewrite.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] get never hands out a leased, dirty, in-use, or Destroying worktree
- [ ] A reused worktree is reset to the latest default branch (branchRef: prefer-ahead/local, origin on divergence)
- [ ] release clears owner + lease and returns the worktree to available; conditional release is ABA-safe exactly-once
- [ ] status heals + writes state under the lock, and classifies into exactly the 5 Go statuses
- [ ] A dirty-prompt decline path exists at the CLI layer (not core)
- [ ] The 'you're here' status only when cwd is inside the worktree
- [ ] NO git/hooks/process work runs under the state lock (short-lock target)

title: Implement pool destroy (two-phase, safe-by-default)
description:
## Background
Go destroy (internal/pool/destroy.go) is safe-by-default: dry-run unless --yes, narrow explicit targets, each risk class its own --include-* opt-in, NO cross-pool/global destroy, leased never removed by --all, two-phase reservation. This is the v2.0.0 contract the port MUST reproduce.

## Technical Approach
- struct DestroyOptions { dry_run, include_unlanded, include_in_use, include_leased, pre_destroy: Vec<String> }
- struct DestroyTarget { name, path, bytes: u64, class: DestroyClass, classes: Vec<DestroyClass>, processes: Vec<ProcessInfo>, detail: String }
- struct DestroySkip { target, needed_flags: Vec<&'static str>, leased_bulk: bool, detail }
- struct DestroyResult { dry_run, all, scope, planned: Vec<DestroyTarget>, destroyed, skipped, planned_bytes, freed_bytes }
- destroy_worktree(pool, path, opts): single named path; allow_leased = true (named path + --include-leased may remove a lease).
- destroy_pool(pool, opts): bulk --all; allow_leased = FALSE (leased NEVER removable by --all regardless of flag; skip marked LeasedBulk).
- classify then opts.allows(target, allow_leased): missing_flags == [] -> removable; else skip with NeededFlag(s).
- TWO-PHASE execute (dry_run skips this entirely):
  - Phase 1 (with_state_lock): read+heal; for each planned path, classify with live state; if already Destroying + live owner -> skip 'reserved by another destroy'; stamp Destroying=true + reserve_owner(fresh pair) + save ORIGINAL pair into Reservation::Destroy; WriteState.
  - Hooks OUTSIDE all locks: pre_destroy hooks in the worktree dir (non-fatal).
  - Phase 2 (fresh with_state_lock): re-locate; Reservation::matches() (Path + Destroying + OwnerPID + OwnerStartedAt); re-run classify; if entry missing / token broken / reclassified un-gated -> SKIP and restore_original (never delete a re-acquired worktree). If in-use and include_in_use: terminate processes (2s grace); survivors -> restore + skip. Then git worktree remove --force -> RemoveAll container (guarded by removable_worktree_container) -> clear reservation -> WriteState.
- measure_size: dirSize of the numbered container.
- Error cases (exit 1): --include-leased cannot be combined with --all; --all requires a pool path; no path and no --all; 'worktree <path> is not managed by treehouse'; cannot resolve pool. Single-target: dry-run -> 0; executed with >=1 destroyed -> 0; executed 0 destroyed + skip -> CommandError::SingleDestroySkipped (did not destroy <name> (<class>); re-run with <flags>), LeasedBulk skipped. Bulk --all skips are normal -> 0.

## Success Criteria
- Dry-run by default, risk-revealing preview ([disposable]/[leased]/[in-use:<pid>]/[dirty]/[unmerged]/[unverified] tags, size, path)
- No cross-pool/global destroy; --all without a pool path errors
- Leased worktrees never removed by --all (even with --include-leased + --yes); only exact path + --include-leased
- Combined classes require every flag; a re-acquired worktree (mid-hook) is never deleted
- Original owner reservation restored on every skip; destroy and prune classify the same fixture identically
- Never prints a blind 'All worktrees destroyed'

## Test Plan
- Port Go internal/pool tests + e2e: TestDestroyDryRunByDefault, TestDestroySpecificWithYes, TestDestroyDirtyRequiresIncludeUnlanded, TestDestroyAllRemovesPoolAndIsScopedToIt, TestDestroyAllFromManagedWorktreeSubdirUsesMainRepoPool, TestDestroyAllRequiresPoolTarget, TestDestroyAllNeverRemovesLeasedWorktree, TestDestroyLeasedSinglePathWithIncludeLeased, TestDestroySpecificSkipsWhenCallerStillInWorktree, TestDestroyNoArgs
- Unit: classification gates (from worktree.rs bead), two-phase re-verify, hook-dirtying re-classify, reservation restore
- Concurrency: concurrent destroy + acquire; re-acquire during hook

## Considerations
- Reuse the shared classify + two-phase engine for prune/gc (same primitives).
- 'did not destroy' is a CommandError rendered by the CLI, not a result.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Dry-run by default, risk-revealing preview ([disposable]/[leased]/[in-use:<pid>]/[dirty]/[unmerged]/[unverified] tags, size, path)
- [ ] No cross-pool/global destroy; --all without a pool path errors

title: Implement pool prune (stale, dry-run default, orphans opt-in)
description:
## Background
Go prune (internal/pool/prune.go) removes only stale idle managed worktrees that are clean and whose HEAD is merged into the default ref. Dry-run is default. It supports --yes, --all/--global (sweep every pool under user-level root, from anywhere), --prune-orphans (backing-repo-missing), --verbose. Prune NEVER deletes a leased worktree, an in-use worktree, an unmerged/dirty one, or an origin-unreachable one.

## Technical Approach
- struct PruneOptions { dry_run, prune_orphans, pre_destroy }
- struct PruneWorktree { name, path, bytes: u64, orphaned: bool, warning: String }
- struct PruneSkipped { name, path, category: String, reason: String, detail: String }
- struct PruneResult { candidates, pruned, skipped, reclaimable_bytes, freed_bytes }
- struct PruneAllResult { pool_root, pools: Vec<PrunePoolResult>, total: PruneResult }
- resolve_prune_default_ref(repo_root) -> Result<String, PruneVerificationError>: FETCH origin FIRST (no-op without origin); then default_branch_merge_ref; failure categorized (OriginUnreachable vs cannot-verify) as a SKIP, never a deletion. Local-only repos use refs/heads/<default>.
- prune_pool / prune_all: snapshot under one lock (read+heal+WriteState); per entry analyze_prune_candidate (skip Destroying/Leased/owner_alive/in-use early) then analyze_idle_worktree (orphan/dirty/merged/size). Dry-run: report candidates + bytes, NO reservation.
- execute: reuse the shared two-phase engine (phase 1 reserve Destroying + owner, hooks OUTSIDE, phase 2 re-verify sameDestroyReservation -> git worktree remove (plain, clean) -> RemoveAll container -> clear reservation). Any skip restores original owner.
- Message strings (human, stdout, all prefixed tree emoji) exactly matching Go (byte-exact for scripts): 'No stale worktrees to prune.', 'Dry run: would prune <n> stale worktree(s) and reclaim <bytes>.', 'Re-run with --yes to delete these worktrees.', 'Pruned <n> stale worktree(s) and freed <bytes>.', global variants append 'across <n> pool(s).', 'Skipped <n> unsafe idle worktree(s):' grouped by category, orphan hint 'Re-run with --prune-orphans ...'.
- Skip categories exact strings: uncommitted changes, unmerged, orphaned (backing repository missing), origin unreachable (cannot verify), cannot verify worktree, cannot check processes, cannot measure size, cleanup failed, remove failed, in use. Orphan warning: content could not be verified.
- format_bytes: <1024 -> 'N B'; else 1024-step KiB/MiB/GiB/TiB, one decimal, trailing zeros and dot trimmed.
- prune rejects positional args (cobra NoArgs).

## Success Criteria
- Prune only removes disposable (merged+clean+idle+unleased) worktrees; dry-run default
- Fetches origin first; uses remote-tracking default ref (not local shadowing origin, not stale origin/HEAD)
- Origin unreachable -> category-tagged skip, never deletion, even with --prune-orphans
- Orphans only deletable with --prune-orphans --yes; each warns 'content could not be verified'
- Leased worktrees silently skipped (never candidates)
- Two-phase engine reused; re-acquired worktree never deleted; original owner restored on skip
- All 9 commands' human output byte-matches Go where verified by Go tests

- Port Go internal/pool tests + e2e: TestPruneDryRunAndYes, TestPruneAllDryRunAndYesAcrossPoolsFromAnywhere, TestPruneMixedStaleAndSkippedOrphanPrintsOrphanHints, TestPruneAllReportsOrphanWithoutRawGitErrorsAndPrunesOnlyWithExplicitFlag, TestPruneAllDoesNotDeleteOriginUnreachableWithPruneOrphans, TestPruneAllYesRecoversCorruptPool, TestPruneWithoutAllScopesToCurrentRepo, TestPruneRejectsPositionalArgs, TestPruneEmptyPoolDoesNotRequireOrigin, TestPruneSkipsUnsafeWorktrees, TestPruneRefreshesOriginBeforeMergeSafety, TestPruneUsesCurrentRemoteDefaultBranch
- Unit: format_bytes golden cases, skip category grouping/ordering

## Considerations
- prune keeps its Go contract: leased entries silently skipped (stale leases included). Only gc (P1) surfaces valid/stale leases.
- Raw git diagnostics suppressed unless --verbose.

## Acceptance Criteria

title: Implement process detection + termination (process.rs)
description:
## Background
Go internal/process/detect.go uses gopsutil to find processes whose cwd is inside a worktree (in-use detection) and terminate.go terminates lingering processes (SIGTERM->SIGKILL on unix, TerminateProcess on Windows). The port uses sysinfo 0.39.6 for cross-platform process enumeration.

## Technical Approach
- struct ProcessInfo { pid: i32, name: String } with Display "name (pid)".
- ProcessTable wrapping sysinfo::System (Mutex): refresh_processes() then query. Methods:
  - find_in_worktree(worktree_path) -> Result<Vec<ProcessInfo>>: enumerate processes; for each, cwd() -> Option<&Path>; resolve symlinks (EvalSymlinks) on both worktree path and cwd (macOS /tmp -> /private/tmp; symlinked worktree paths); include if rel(cwd, wt) == "." or a descendant; include children whose dir name literally starts with ".." (e.g. ..cache) — the Go matcher is: rel == "." || (rel != ".." && !starts_with ".."+sep).
  - started_at(pid) -> (i64, bool): epoch time. IMPORTANT: Go stores gopsutil CreateTime in epoch MILLIS; sysinfo start_time() returns epoch SECONDS. Multiply by 1000 to store millis (accept truncation) so owner_alive matches across the mixed Go+Rust window. Document that mixed-pool concurrency is unsupported (risk #2).
  - exists(pid) -> bool (PidExists analog)
  - terminate_with_grace(worktree_path, grace: Duration) -> Result<Vec<ProcessInfo>>:
    - find_in_worktree, then filter protected: the calling process AND its whole ancestor chain must NEVER be killed (walk ppid up; a parent-lookup failure fails CLOSED — terminate nothing).
    - unix: SIGTERM all -> wait up to grace polling every 50ms -> SIGKILL survivors. Grace >= 400ms per Go test.
    - windows: TerminateProcess (abrupt; no graceful equivalent). gracePeriod is effectively ignored on Windows (Go parity). Survivors -> ProcessError::Survived.
- ProcessError enum: NoStartTime(i32), Scan(String), Survived(i32).

## Success Criteria
- In-use detection matches by resolved realpath (symlinks OK)
- Children with dir names starting ".." are detected
- Termination never kills self or ancestors; parent-lookup failure terminates nothing
- SIGTERM then escalate to SIGKILL only after grace; already-dead PIDs are no-ops
- Windows termination covers the path (processes terminated, no self-kill) even though abrupt

## Test Plan
- Port Go internal/process/detect_unix_test.go + terminate_unix_test.go (spawn real sleep / sh -c 'trap "" TERM; sleep 60'; 200ms settle; NOT parallel)
- Unit: filter_protected_processes logic; path resolution with symlinks; Windows termination smoke test
- NOTE these are timing-sensitive and can flake in CI; keep settle sleeps, mark them.

## Considerations
- sysinfo must be refreshed before querying (System::new_all or refresh_processes).
- cwd() returns None for exited/permission-restricted processes — skip them.
- The most expensive check in the whole tool; gc/doctor sweep uses it per worktree.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] In-use detection matches by resolved realpath (symlinks OK)
- [ ] Children with dir names starting ".." are detected
- [ ] Termination never kills self or ancestors; parent-lookup failure terminates nothing
- [ ] SIGTERM then escalate to SIGKILL only after grace; already-dead PIDs are no-ops
- [ ] Windows termination covers the path (processes terminated, no self-kill) even though abrupt

title: Implement Reservation token (reservation.rs): owner + two-phase destroy
description:
## Background
Go owner reservations are the {OwnerPID, OwnerStartedAt} pair (internal/pool/pool.go reserveOwner, ownerAlive). Destroy uses a two-phase reservation: stamp Destroying=true + fresh owner pair, record the ORIGINAL pair, run hooks outside the lock, then re-verify under a fresh lock and delete only if the reservation still matches (sameDestroyReservation). Any skip restores the original reservation. The Rust port models this as a Reservation token that is PERSISTED in the state file so it survives lock releases.

## Technical Approach
- struct Reservation { worktree: String, kind: ReservationKind }
- enum ReservationKind:
  - Owner { owner_pid: i32, owner_started_at: i64 }
  - Destroy { owner_pid: i32, owner_started_at: i64, original_owner_pid: i32, original_owner_started_at: i64 }
  - Lease(Lease)
- impl Reservation:
  - matches(&self, entry) -> bool: sameDestroyReservation — Path matches, Destroying==true, OwnerPID==, OwnerStartedAt==. For Owner/Lease: re-read entry and compare persisted identity fields.
  - restore_original(&self, entry): Destroying=false, restore original owner pair (skip-path repair).
  - reserve_owner(&self, process) -> Result: stamp OwnerPID=os::getpid(), OwnerStartedAt=started_at_ms(pid); error if undeterminable.
- pub fn owner_alive(entry, process) -> bool: BOTH fields non-zero AND process.started_at(pid) == owner_started_at (PID-reuse protected: a recycled PID has a different start time).
- heal_state clears a dead owner: owner_pid!=0 && !owner_alive -> OwnerPID=0, OwnerStartedAt=0, Destroying=false. It also drops vanished paths. NEVER touches lease fields.

## Success Criteria
- owner_alive requires both fields AND matching start time (PID-reuse ABA safe)
- Reservation::matches is the exact analog of sameDestroyReservation
- restore_original exactly restores the pre-destroy owner state
- A dead owner's reservation self-heals on the next status/gc/run

## Test Plan
- Unit: owner_alive with dead pid, recycled pid (different start time), zero fields; matches; restore_original
- Port Go internal/pool tests covering owner reservation heal + PID-reuse
- Concurrency: two-phase destroy re-verify (see destroy bead) — a worktree re-acquired mid-hook is never deleted

## Considerations
- OwnerStartedAt precision: store MILLIS (Go uses gopsutil CreateTime millis; sysinfo start_time() is seconds — multiply by 1000). Cross-tool precision mismatch is risk #2.
- The reservation IS the anti-TOCTOU wall during the short-lock protocol (P1-A hardening formalizes it).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] owner_alive requires both fields AND matching start time (PID-reuse ABA safe)
- [ ] Reservation::matches is the exact analog of sameDestroyReservation
- [ ] restore_original exactly restores the pre-destroy owner state
- [ ] A dead owner's reservation self-heals on the next status/gc/run

title: P1-D: treehouse run -- <cmd> (cleanup-always, signal forwarding, TTL backstop)
description:
## Background
treehouse run -- <cmd...> is the killer feature for the pain point: acquire -> spawn agent -> cleanup ALWAYS on every exit path -> never a permanent leak. It is P1-D, implemented LAST because it leans on the primitives stabilized by P0..P1-C (acquire/lease/release + gc).

## Technical Approach
- struct RunOptions { command: Vec<OsString>, ttl: Duration, holder: String }
- enum CleanupOutcome { Cleaned, CleanupFailed(String) }
- struct RunResult { worktree_path: PathBuf, lease_id: String, lease_holder: String, child_exit_code: Option<i32>, child_signal: Option<i32>, cleanup: CleanupOutcome }
- run(repo_root, pool_dir, cfg, opts) -> Result<RunResult>:
  1. ACQUIRE: internal lease acquire (get --lease semantics, hook stdout routed to stderr), holder = 'run:<pid>' (or --lease-holder / TREEHOUSE_LEASE_HOLDER override), TTL = --ttl > config lease_ttl > 24h default. The lease is load-bearing: process-independent + TTL-bounded, so even a SIGKILLed treehouse leaves a self-expiring reservation rather than an eternal one.
  2. SPAWN: child env gets TREEHOUSE_DIR=<abs wt> + TREEHOUSE_LEASE_ID=<lease_id> (so the child/harness can return --if-lease-id); cwd = worktree; stdio inherited; spawned directly (no shell) in a NEW PROCESS GROUP (setpgid unix / CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP windows).
  3. CLEANUP-ALWAYS (RAII Drop guard): on EVERY exit path — normal exit, nonzero exit, signal, treehouse-side error, unwinding panic — detach HEAD, reset to default ref, terminate lingering processes (2s grace, SIGTERM->SIGKILL / TerminateProcess), release the lease. A nonzero child exit is NOT a reason to leak. Cleanup failure -> warning 'failed to clean worktree'.
  4. SIGNAL FORWARDING: unix — install SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP handlers; forward to the child's whole process group (kill(-pgid, sig)); wait for child; cleanup; exit 128+signum. Windows — GenerateConsoleCtrlEvent(CTRL_BREAK_EVENT, pgid) / graceful TerminateProcess fallback; wait; cleanup.
  5. EXIT CODE: run exits with the child's exit code (0-255; unix signal -> 128+signum). treehouse run -- false -> 1; -- true -> 0. Spawn failure / pool exhausted -> error, exit 1. Cleanup failure still returns the child's code but warns loudly.
- NO PERMANENT LEAK IF TREEHOUSE IS SIGKILLED (uncatchable, no Drop): the TTL lease is still valid in state -> status shows 'leased (held by run:<pid>)' -> after expiry it's STALE and a later gc --all --yes (cron) reclaims it iff idle+clean+merged; if the orphaned child is still running, gc skips it as 'in use' and status/doctor surface it until the child exits or a human runs destroy --include-in-use --yes. Guarantee: a lease can never block a pool slot longer than (TTL + next gc sweep), and a live agent is never evicted.

## Success Criteria
- Cleanup runs on EVERY exit path (exit 0, nonzero, signal, panic)
- Exit code = child's code; signals forwarded to the child's process group
- SIGKILLed treehouse leaves a TTL-bounded lease (no eternal leak); gc reclaims after expiry if idle
- A live agent past TTL is never evicted (in-use check)
- Child can release via TREEHOUSE_LEASE_ID

## Test Plan
- e2e: run -- true (exit 0, worktree returned), run -- false (exit 1, worktree returned), run -- sleep+sigint (signal forwarded, cleanup, 128+signum), run -- long-process then SIGKILL treehouse (state shows leased, gc reclaims after expiry if idle)
- Unit: RAII cleanup guard fires on panic; signal handler wiring (unix)
- Port harness: use real child processes with controlled exits

## Considerations
- run's cleanup is best-effort on panic=abort/SIGKILL; the TTL lease is the backstop. Orphaned child keeping disk is a process lifetime, not a state leak.
- Windows: GenerateConsoleCtrlEvent + TerminateProcess fallback; no SIGTERM.
- Implement LAST (P1-D) — it depends on the stable acquire/lease/release + gc primitives.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Cleanup runs on EVERY exit path (exit 0, nonzero, signal, panic)
- [ ] Exit code = child's code; signals forwarded to the child's process group
- [ ] SIGKILLed treehouse leaves a TTL-bounded lease (no eternal leak); gc reclaims after expiry if idle
- [ ] A live agent past TTL is never evicted (in-use check)
- [ ] Child can release via TREEHOUSE_LEASE_ID

title: Implement lock.rs (with_state_lock, exclusive fd-lock + timeout)
description:
## Background
Go serializes all state read-modify-write under WithStateLock on <poolDir>/treehouse-state.lock (flock LOCK_EX unix / LockFileEx windows). The port must reproduce the EXCLUSIVE-lock semantics. Per the plan review, do NOT build a read/write lock abstraction — fd-lock's Mutex (exclusive) is sufficient; status also needs exclusive because it heals + writes.

## Technical Approach
- with_state_lock(pool_dir, f) -> Result<T, Error>: MkdirAll(pool_dir, 0755); open <poolDir>/treehouse-state.lock O_CREATE|O_RDWR 0644; acquire exclusive lock via fd_lock::Mutex::lock() (flock LOCK_EX unix / LockFileEx whole-file windows); run f; unlock on Drop (explicitly even on error/panic).
- Lock TIMEOUT (port addition): Go blocks forever; implement try_lock + retry/backoff up to lock_timeout, returning StateError::LockTimeout. Document the default (research suggests a few seconds). Do not assume infinite blocking in parity tests.
- The lock file's existence creates the pool dir.
- Advisory only (cooperative processes). Windows locks are not inherited by children; second handle in same process doesn't contend — drop explicitly.
- fd-lock pins windows-sys >=0.52,<0.60; we also use windows-sys 0.61.2 directly => two copies build. Harmless; add a Cargo.toml comment so nobody 'fixes' it.

## Success Criteria
- Two processes cannot interleave read-modify-write
- Lock acquisition with a wedged holder times out with LockTimeout (not infinite block)
- Lock released on Drop/error/panic

## Test Plan
- Unit + integration: two goroutine/thread or two subprocess writers serialize; timeout path; lock released after panic (thread).
- Concurrency/race tests belong with the P1 hardening bead, but basic mutual exclusion is P0.

## Considerations
- This is the single most important invariant to port: read-modify-write atomicity requires the whole read+mutate+write inside ONE with_state_lock.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Two processes cannot interleave read-modify-write
- [ ] Lock acquisition with a wedged holder times out with LockTimeout (not infinite block)
- [ ] Lock released on Drop/error/panic

title: Implement state.rs (Go wire-compatible State + WorktreeEntry + heal)
description:
## Background
treehouse-core/src/state.rs holds the persisted pool state. The Go baseline (internal/pool/state.go, read from .tmp/treehouse/) defines the wire format that a Rust port MUST reproduce exactly (snake_case, omitempty/omitzero). This is the single most load-bearing file for compatibility.

## Technical Approach
- struct State { #[serde(default)] worktrees: Vec<WorktreeEntry> }
- struct WorktreeEntry with serde rename_all = "snake_case" (NOT camelCase — plan §4.3 warning): name:String, path:String, created_at (rfc3339_nano shim), destroying:bool (skip_serializing_if is_false), owner_pid:i32 (skip is_zero_i32), owner_started_at:i64 (skip is_zero_i64), leased:bool (skip is_false), lease_id:String (skip is_empty_str), lease_holder:String (skip is_empty_str), leased_at (skip is_zero_utc). P1 additive: expires_at (skip is_zero_utc; zero = permanent lease).
- Go zero-time sentinel is year-1 0001-01-01T00:00:00Z; Rust uses DateTime::<Utc>::UNIX_EPOCH as the zero sentinel. rfc3339_nano serde shim: serialize trims sub-second when 0, else full nano, parseable by Go; deserialize accepts Go RFC3339Nano incl. year-1 zero time.
- Missing keys decode to zero via #[serde(default)]. A missing state file = fresh empty pool. A 0-byte file is CORRUPT (not missing) — triggers recovery, never a fresh pool.
- impl WorktreeEntry::is_stale_lease(now) = leased && !zero(expires_at) && now >= expires_at; is_valid_lease(now) = leased && (zero(expires_at) || now < expires_at). (P1, but land the fields now with additive serde.)
- read_state(pool_dir): missing => State{worktrees:[]}; unparsable => recover_corrupt_state; else parse.
- heal_state(&mut State): clear dead owner reservations (owner_pid != 0 && process_started_at(pid) != owner_started_at => zero owner + destroying=false), DROP entries whose path no longer exists, NEVER touch any lease field (valid or stale).
- clear_lease(wt): leased=false, id/holder="", leased_at=zero, expires_at=zero.
- owner_alive(wt): owner_pid != 0 && owner_started_at != 0 && process_started_at(pid) == owner_started_at.
- new_lease_id(): 16 random bytes => 32 lowercase hex (rand getrandom).

## Success Criteria
- State round-trips Go-format JSON byte-compatible (field names + presence)
- Pre-lease state file (no lease keys) loads as Leased=false, empty IDs
- A 0-byte file triggers recovery, not fresh
- heal_state never touches lease fields
- Unit tests cover each serde omission rule

## Test Plan
- Unit: serialize/deserialize golden JSON incl. omitempty cases, empty-file vs missing-file, heal behavior, clear_lease, is_stale_lease boundary
- Mirror Go internal/pool/state_test.go + e2e TestPruneAllYesRecoversCorruptPool

## Considerations
- The design sketch in plan §4.3 shows camelCase but the NOTE under it is authoritative: use snake_case.
- OwnerStartedAt precision: Go uses gopsutil CreateTime epoch millis; sysinfo start_time() is epoch seconds. Store millis (accept truncation) — see risks #2/#4.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] State round-trips Go-format JSON byte-compatible (field names + presence)
- [ ] Pre-lease state file (no lease keys) loads as Leased=false, empty IDs
- [ ] A 0-byte file triggers recovery, not fresh
- [ ] heal_state never touches lease fields
- [ ] Unit tests cover each serde omission rule
