title: P1-C: Stale leases (--ttl) + treehouse gc + crash-recovery surfacing
description:
## Background
The #1 pain: agents acquire worktrees, then crash or forget to return them, leaking worktrees and filling disk. P1-C adds stale-lease detection (expires_at + --ttl) and treehouse gc (safe reclaim), plus crash-recovery surfacing. A valid lease is NEVER auto-reclaimed; only an EXPIRED lease that also passes the full disposable bar is reclaimed by gc.

## Technical Approach
- STATE: WorktreeEntry gains expires_at (omitempty/omitzero; zero = permanent lease, so pre-P1 state files load identically). is_stale_lease(now) = leased && !zero(expires_at) && now >= expires_at; is_valid_lease(now) = leased && (zero(expires_at) || now < expires_at). heal_state NEVER clears any lease (valid or stale); stale leases are surfaced, not un-leased.
- GET --LEASE --TTL: humantime duration (30m, 1h30m, 24h). --ttl requires --lease (error); --ttl > 0. TREEHOUSE_LEASE_TTL env fallback. LeaseInfo gains 5th field expires_at (always present, null when permanent). status human appends '(expired)' to stale leased rows; status --json adds per-element expires_at (null) + stale (bool) — ADDITIVE, no existing key changes.
- treehouse gc: flags --yes, --all/--global, --prune-orphans, --verbose/-v; NoArgs; DRY-RUN by default. Cleans: (1) heal dead-owner reservations + drop vanished paths; (2) candidates: stale-lease pass disposable bar -> '[stale lease]'; ordinary idle spares -> '[stale]' (prune's analysis); backing-repo-missing orphans -> skipped unless --prune-orphans -> '[stale/orphaned]'; VALID leases -> NEVER candidates (distinct skip category 'valid lease'); recovered-from-corrupt (no expires_at) -> permanent -> never gc'd; (3) dry-run classify+measure+sort+report; (4) execute --yes reuses the shared two-phase destroy (reserve -> hooks OUTSIDE -> re-verify sameDestroyReservation -> remove). gc has NO --include-* flags (strictly safe).
- GC MESSAGE STRINGS (stdout, tree emoji, mirror prune): 'No stale worktrees to reclaim.', 'Dry run: would reclaim <n> worktree(s) and free <bytes>.', 'Re-run with --yes to reclaim these worktrees.', 'Reclaimed <n> worktree(s) and freed <bytes>.', 'Skipped <n> worktree(s):' + category groups, orphan hint 'Re-run with --prune-orphans ...'. format_bytes identical.
- CRASH RECOVERY SURFACING: status/doctor detect: dead owner (heal auto-clears; PID-reuse safe), expired lease (surfaced, reclaimable only by gc/explicit), corrupt state (recover conservatively, holder placeholder, NO expires_at so gc never auto-reclaims). A stale-lease worktree that is dirty/unmerged/in-use is SKIPPED by gc and its lease NOT cleared (a human force-recovers with return --force or destroy --include-leased --include-unlanded).
- SECOND SAFETY LAYER: even a live agent running past TTL is protected — its live process makes it 'in use', so gc skips it. TTL only unblocks idle worktrees.

## Success Criteria
- get --lease --ttl records expires_at; a valid lease is never auto-reclaimed (get/prune/gc/bulk destroy --all all skip it)
- gc dry-runs by default, reclaims only disposable (expired+idle+clean+merged+backing-present) worktrees, uses the shared two-phase engine
- Stale leases surfaced in status/doctor, never silently cleared; corrupt-recovered entries never auto-reclaimed
- A live agent past TTL is never evicted (in-use check)
- --format json/toon supported by gc (P1-B output layer)

## Test Plan
- Unit: is_stale_lease/is_valid_lease boundaries; gc candidate gating (expired+dirty skip, valid lease skip, expired+disposable candidate)
- e2e: get --lease --ttl; gc dry-run vs --yes; gc --all; gc never removes valid lease or live agent; corrupt pool not gc'd
- status --json additive fields (expires_at/stale) don't break existing field-set consumers

## Considerations
- Clock skew: expires_at written by acquiring machine, compared by gc machine; pool is local so negligible (documented).
- Windows RemoveAll on in-use files can fail after git worktree remove --force -> 'remove failed' skip, stale lease persists until process exits or human recovers — no data loss.
- Contract extension of LeaseInfo/status JSON is additive; re-validate exact-field-set consumers.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] get --lease --ttl records expires_at; a valid lease is never auto-reclaimed (get/prune/gc/bulk destroy --all all skip it)
- [ ] gc dry-runs by default, reclaims only disposable (expired+idle+clean+merged+backing-present) worktrees, uses the shared two-phase engine
- [ ] Stale leases surfaced in status/doctor, never silently cleared; corrupt-recovered entries never auto-reclaimed
- [ ] A live agent past TTL is never evicted (in-use check)
- [ ] --format json/toon supported by gc (P1-B output layer)

title: Implement updater subsystem (treehouse update + --update-check background check)
description:
## Background
Go has a full self-update subsystem (internal/updater/): a background version check + a `treehouse update` command that downloads the release asset, verifies sha256, and atomically replaces the executable. The Go CLI wires this as: PersistentPreRun checks the cache (~/.treehouse/update-check.json, 24h TTL) and spawns a detached `--update-check <version>` child; `update` does the download/verify/replace. The Rust port must reproduce this subsystem. This is a separate, self-contained subsystem — it does NOT depend on the pool/state/git core.

## Technical Approach
- internal/updater equivalent: treehouse-core module `updater` (or a treehouse-updater feature) — keep it isolated from pool/state.
- VERSION CHECK: hit GitHub API latest release (default https://api.github.com/repos/kunchenguid/treehouse/releases/latest; overridable in tests via an injected base URL + HTTPS-enforcement toggle). Compare semver (pre-release < release; parse major.minor.patch[-prerelease]); cache entry {"checked_at": RFC3339, "latest_version": string} at ~/.treehouse/update-check.json, TTL 24h. IsCacheStale: cache older than TTL, missing, OR cached latest <= current.
- BACKGROUND CHECK: hidden `--update-check <version>` arg intercepted in main BEFORE clap. Spawn a detached child (nix Setsid on unix / CREATE_NEW_PROCESS_GROUP on Windows), stdio nulled, env TREEHOUSE_NO_UPDATE_CHECK=1 to prevent recursion; child does best-effort check + writes cache + exits 0 (no version arg -> exit 1). Parent fires-and-forgets (no wait).
- UPDATE COMMAND: `treehouse update`. dev build -> 'Skipping update: running a dev build' (exit 0). Else CheckLatest; no update -> 'treehouse is up to date (<version>)' (exit 0). Update available -> download the matching asset (treehouse-v<ver>-<os>-<arch>.tar.gz / .zip on Windows) + checksums.txt, verify sha256 of the archive, extract the binary, strip macOS quarantine xattr (best-effort), atomically replace the executable (temp in same dir + rename; fallback direct overwrite if the dir isn't writable). HTTPS enforced on all download URLs. All update output goes to STDOUT (matching Go's fmt.Println). 'Successfully updated treehouse <old> -> <new>' green.
- Skip the PersistentPreRun update-check for the update command itself, for dev builds, and when TREEHOUSE_NO_UPDATE_CHECK == '1'.
- CACHE READ: PersistentPreRun shows a yellow notice to stderr when the cache says update available: 'A new version of treehouse is available: <v> -> <v>' + 'Run "treehouse update" to update' + blank line.

## Success Criteria
- Background check + cache (24h TTL) + notice behavior matches Go
- update downloads + verifies sha256 + atomically replaces the executable; HTTPS enforced
- --update-check child is detached, silent, non-recursive (env guard)
- Dev build skips update; TREEHOUSE_NO_UPDATE_CHECK == '1' disables the machinery
- Update messages byte-match Go on stdout

## Test Plan
- Port Go internal/updater/updater_test.go: version ordering (semver incl. pre-release), asset name per platform, checksum verify (sha256), HTTPS enforcement, cache staleness
- e2e against a local HTTP server (inject base URL + disable HTTPS in tests): check, download, verify, replace
- macOS quarantine removal is best-effort; test the happy path only

## Considerations
- GitHub API responses and release asset names are the contract; keep the URL/configurable-in-test seams (github_api_url, enforce_https vars like Go).
- Atomic replace: temp file in the SAME dir as the target (same filesystem) then rename; if the dir isn't writable (e.g. /usr/local/bin owned by root) fall back to direct overwrite (non-atomic, documented).
- This subsystem has NO dependency on the pool/state/git core — parallelize it with core module work.
- Depends on the CLI commands bead (flag/dispatch wiring) + the workspace scaffold.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Background check + cache (24h TTL) + notice behavior matches Go
- [ ] update downloads + verifies sha256 + atomically replaces the executable; HTTPS enforced
- [ ] --update-check child is detached, silent, non-recursive (env guard)
- [ ] Dev build skips update; TREEHOUSE_NO_UPDATE_CHECK == '1' disables the machinery
- [ ] Update messages byte-match Go on stdout
